text: DSH Tool Config Studio（DSH 网页插件）：在侧栏提供工具配置和系统插件设置面板。它通过 DSH 客户端注册两个面板，供用户浏览已注册工具、搜索工具与参数、调整可保存的默认配置，并查看或编辑系统插件开放的档案级设置。工具侧支持启用或停用、参数校验、单项重置和恢复全部默认值；系统侧支持编辑、暂存、保存及恢复设置。适合希望在界面中管理 DSH 工具默认值或系统插件参数的用户。无需额外 API Key；工具覆盖默认保存在浏览器 localStorage，系统设置经 DSH Host 接口读写。

dsh-tool-config-studio README · DSH Tool Config Studio：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) bundle that turns the tool catalog **and the system settings document** into settings surfaces: **browse every registered tool or system plugin, expand any of them to edit its configuration, and — when you've made a mistake — restore the defaults with a single click.** Installs as a proper DSH plugin from the Plugins page and adds two panels to the sidebar: *Tool Config Studio* (tool defaults) and *System Plugin Studio* (model adapters, default model, and every other plugin that exposes live-editable parameters).

dsh-tool-config-studio README · Why：Every DSH tool takes parameters, and a meaningful share of them have tunable, *stored* behavior: how far `read` goes by default, whether `pwsh` jobs run in the background, which scope `list_agents` starts from, how `job_output` waits, the minimum interval a schedule may tick, and so on. Before, the only way to discover or change those defaults was to dig through source or profile patches. Tool Config Studio gives each tool a proper settings page, and — more importantly — guarantees you can always undo a change.

dsh-tool-config-studio README · Why：The system side of things was even less visible: the model adapter (`llm-pi-ai` providers and models), the profile's `llm-deepseek` adapter, and the active `agent-default-model` all live in the profile's settings document, editable only by hand in YAML. The **System Plugin Studio** panel reads that document live, renders a form for every parameter a plugin exposes as *volatile* (editable per profile), and edits it back through the Host — with the same staged-then-flushed discipline and one-click restore as the tool side.

dsh-tool-config-studio README · Features：- **Full tool catalog** — all 31 registered tools, grouped into 11 categories, each with a description and a complete parameter reference (type, required flag, default, enum values, minimums).
- **Stored-default editing** — expand any tool and change its configurable parameters: numbers with minimums, booleans, free strings, and enum selects.
- **Enable / disable** — toggle a tool on or off with a switch.
- **Inline validation** — every value is validated against the catalog (type, enum membership, minimum bounds) *before* it is stored. Invalid input never persists; the error is shown right next to the field.
- **Restore at every level** — reset a single parameter, restore one tool to factory state, or **Restore all defaults** (with confirmation). The store keeps only *deviations* from the catalog, so restoring is an exact inverse and can never lose anything else.
- **System Plugin Studio panel** — a second sidebar/main panel that scans the live DSH settings document and renders a schema-driven form for every system plugin whose parameters are *volatile* (editable per profile): model adapters, the active model, and friends. Dictionaries, arr

dsh-tool-config-studio README · Install in DSH (desktop or web)：This package is a **DSH bundle** — install it from the Plugins page:

1. Open **Plugins** in the DSH sidebar → **Add plugin**.
2. Paste the repository URL: `https://github.com/yqd-coder/dsh-tool-config-studio.git`
3. Confirm. The plugin manager fetches the repo, installs it into your profile, and enables the bundle — a **Tool Config Studio** entry appears in the sidebar, and the bundle row (toggleable) is listed under Plugins.
dsh-tool-config-studio README · Install in DSH (desktop or web)：Uninstalling or toggling the bundle off removes the panel; your stored configuration (localStorage) is kept.

npm test
```

The suite uses Node's built-in test runner (`node --test test/`) — no framework, no installation step. 83 tests cover catalog integrity, the store, validation, persistence, end-to-end UI smoke tests for both panels, the system schema/store/app units, and the built DSH bundle's loader contract — including that `apply` stays re-runnable across a module teardown, the way an in-place plugin update does it.

section: How the DSH bundle is wired

text:
dsh-tool-config-studio README · The configuration model, in 30 seconds：1. **The catalog** (`src/core/catalog.json`) is the single source of truth: every tool, parameter, type, default, enum, and minimum.
2. **The store keeps overrides only** — a value is stored only when it differs from the catalog default; the effective value is `override ?? default`.
3. **Restoring is deleting** — "reset", "restore tool", and "restore all" simply drop overrides, which is the exact inverse of editing.

dsh-tool-config-studio README · The configuration model, in 30 seconds：The full specification — including the storage document format and the validation error codes — is in [docs/configuration-model.md](docs/configuration-model.md).

dsh-tool-config-studio README · The system model, in 30 seconds：1. **The Host owns the settings document** — a layered tree where the system default sits beneath your profile override; `describe()` reports the resolved value, the base, the override, the schema, and a document revision.
2. **Only volatile fields are editable** — a schema field is visible in the panel only when the plugin marks it volatile for the active profile; that is the Host's line between "safe to tune" and "deployment-level".
3. **Editing is an op on a revision** — the panel stages edits locally, then flushes a `mutate` (set/unset ops) or a `replace` (restore) carrying the revision it read; a stale revision is rejected and the panel re-describes.

dsh-tool-config-studio README · The system model, in 30 seconds：> **What the System Plugin Studio cannot touch.** `dsh-persona`, `dsh-system-prompt`, and `dsh-agent-instructions` expose *zero* volatile fields, so personas, system prompts, and agent instructions are not visible or editable in this panel — they are deployment-level settings. The panel shows a note to this effect instead of pretending otherwise.
